text: Coca-Cola tested a new, sweeter formula on nearly two hundred thousand consumers. In blind tests, it beat the old Coke. It even beat Pepsi.
On April 23rd, 1985, the company announced it was replacing its ninety-nine-year-old recipe.
America did not take it well. People stocked up on the old Coke. Protest groups formed. By June, the company's hotline was getting about fifteen hundred calls a day.

The taste tests had asked the wrong question. People weren't just drinking a flavor. They were drinking something they grew up with. Change it, and it felt like the company had taken something that belonged to them.
On July 11th, after seventy-nine days, the original came back as Coca-Cola Classic. In the two days after that announcement, the company got more than thirty-one thousand calls.
New Coke is remembered as one of the biggest marketing mistakes ever. But it showed the company something no taste test could: how much people cared.
